findings.evidence: `Hom.lean:59` defines `weightedEvalHom` with no `@[expose]`, and `Hom.lean:71-72` documents "The body is not exported, so this is how a consumer computes with it". `grep -rn expose TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/WeightedEval/` returns only this line.
findings.fix: Drop `@[expose]` and, as in `Hom.lean`, note in `completionEvalHom_coe`'s docstring that the body is not exported so this is how consumers compute.
findings.issue: `completionEvalHom` carries `@[expose]` although nothing needs its body: `completionEvalHom_coe` (line 66) plus `continuous_completionEvalHom` (line 73) determine it via `UniformSpace.Completion.ext`, and there is no consumer that must unfold or compute with `Completion.extensionHom`.

findings.fix: Extract `completion_weightedRestrictedSubring_ringHom_ext_of_continuous {B} [Semiring B] [TopologicalSpace B] [T2Space B] {f g : Completion (weightedRestrictedSubring T hT) →+* B} (hf hg : Continuous …) (hC hX) : f = g`, proved by `Completion.ext` + `weightedRestrictedSubring_ringHom_ext_of_continuous` on the restrictions along `coeRingHom`, and use it in the `∃!` proof.
findings.issue: The uniqueness principle for the completed algebra — two continuous ring homs out of `Completion (weightedRestrictedSubring T hT)` agreeing on `↑(weightedC …)` and `↑(weightedX …)` are equal — is proved inline (lines 118-129) and reachable publicly only through the `∃!`, which drags in `IsWeightBounded φ T b`, `[CompleteSpace B]`, `[NonarchimedeanRing B]`, `[IsUniformAddGroup B]`, none of which the ext principle needs. The stated downstream use (`A⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩ ≅ A⟨X,Y⟩` via two inverse laws) is exactly an ext application.

findings.issue: The Main-results index says `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion` is "Proposition 5.50 for the completion of `A⟨X⟩_T`" and does not list `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded` at all — contradicting the theorem docstrings (lines 101-103, 134) and reinstating the mislabelling round 1 blocked on.

summary: The characteristic lemma set for `completionEvalHom` is fine, but the definition is `@[expose]`d without need (its sibling `weightedEvalHom` is deliberately unexposed), the reusable uniqueness/ext principle for continuous ring maps out of the completion is proved inline and never exposed, and the module docstring's Main-results index still labels the `IsWeightBounded` theorem as Proposition 5.50 and omits the companion that actually is.
